transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Sofia Nguyen (Redwood AE), Luca Martens (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Arcwell Platform), Daniel Ruiz (Arcwell NetOps), Hannah Lee (Arcwell SecOps), Carlos Mendes (Arcwell SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Week 4 pilot bakeout; discussed regressions after quantization experiment, routing fallback misroutes in cross-region, egress firewall rules blocking telemetry, and agreed on rollback window and runbook distribution.

[00:00] Sofia Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call— can you hear me?
[00:08] Maya Patel: yes, we can. thanks.
[00:10] Sofia Nguyen: Great. Agenda — operational bakeout, routing retune, and the kernel rollback we talked about last week, and then next steps. Luca, you want to start with the latency/quality readout?
[00:22] Luca Martens: Yeah, sure. um, so two quick things up front, we saw two regressions after the mixed-quant path hit production-like load. The first is a small tail-latency bump around 95th percentile, and second is occasional token-stalls that look like a KV-cache invalidation when we fall back between quant8 and float16 shards.
[00:45] Daniel Ruiz: sorry can I interrupt, when you say mixed-quant path — is that the path where some layers got quantized and some are still fp16? we actually saw packet retransmits around the same time, maybe related.
[00:55] Luca Martens: yeah exactly, it's a sharded model mix. sometimes the runtime re-homes cache pointers and some requests hit an invalidated prefix cache which causes a short stall. It's rare but visible under high concurrency.
[01:12] Hannah Lee: is there any chance that's the network jitter not the runtime? our telemetry showed small bursts on the VPC egress at the same timestamps.
[01:21] Luca Martens: great point — we correlated traces; there were a couple of small egress spikes from your NAT gateway which aligned. however the token-stall traces show a stall inside the process where the cache miss triggers a synchronous rebuild. so it's probably a combination.
[01:36] Priya Rao: to be clear, this is the mix that gave Arcwell the 20% token-cost savings, right? we want to keep those gains if possible.
[01:44] Maya Patel: yes, cost is important but latency SLO is higher priority for our clinical flows. a 95th of 350ms is okay but those stalls hitting 700-900ms are not.
[01:55] Sofia Nguyen: Understood. so proposed mitigations: Luca, you proposed temporary rollback to previous kernel that handles mixed shards more conservatively?
[02:04] Luca Martens: yeah. we have a rollback candidate — it's the pre-quant batching kernel that avoids a particular continuous-batching micro-optimization. It's slightly higher steady-state cost but removes the cache-invalidation path. we tested in staging and TTFB improved on the tail.
[02:20] Carlos Mendes: what's the operational risk of the rollback? will it require a full rolling restart or can we do a canary?
[02:27] Luca Martens: rolling restart of the replica set, we can do a staged canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with traffic steering. but you do have to accept a temporary throughput hit during the rollover.
[02:36] Daniel Ruiz: our ops window is Friday night 02:00 UTC. that's the easiest to book. can we keep the rollback reversible?
[02:43] Sofia Nguyen: yes, reversible. we'll escrow the kernel build and have a script to switch back. action item: Luca to prepare rollback runbook and test the rollback on dev cluster.

[03:00] -- Topics: Egress shaping and firewall interactions --
[03:04] Maya Patel: we noticed telemetry packets to Redwood's trace endpoint were being dropped or delayed. our security team tightened egress to only permit a handful of subnets.
[03:15] Hannah Lee: correct. we only allow outbound to a vetted set. can you send the exact FQDNs and IP ranges you expect? the previous doc had redwood.example.com but we need firm IP ranges for our firewall rules.
[03:25] Sofia Nguyen: absolutely, I'll send the network diagram and the ephemeral IP ranges. note that in the console we have a hostname-based certificate rotation — might need CIDR ranges for the CDN endpoints.
[03:36] Priya Rao: also note that our telemetry agent can batch and retry if egress is momentarily blocked. but we saw increased queueing in your staging logs.
[03:44] Carlos Mendes: queueing is the problem; it can backpressure the inference worker if telemetry writethrough blocks.
[03:50] Luca Martens: yep that matches the traces — a stuck telemetry writer held a mutex in a worker thread, leading to small head-of-line blocking. it's an interplay between your egress shaping and our agent.

[04:10] -- Observability gaps --
[04:12] Daniel Ruiz: one ask from our side: can each request emit a persistent trace id so we can correlate NAT translations to the consistent trace? sometimes the trace IDs are short-lived or re-used.
[04:22] Luca Martens: yes, we can surface a request-trace-id header and push it through logs. we already have it internally but we can make it available in the console and wire it to your log collector via the agent.
[04:32] Hannah Lee: please make sure that trace IDs don't include PII. we need to see IDs only, not payloads.
[04:37] Sofia Nguyen: agreed. Redwood will only surface trace metadata — full transcript/payload never leaves unless you enable debug mode.

[05:00] -- Performance experiments & retune suggestions --
[05:04] Luca Martens: short term: two retunes — 1) reduce batch window for low-latency flows (batch cap 8 instead of 16) 2) enable aggressive KV-prefix caching TTL for your clinical flows but keep default for background tasks. These should bring 95th back down.
[05:20] Maya Patel: can we test those in staging without changing quant profile? I'd prefer not to touch quant until after we stabilize.
[05:26] Luca Martens: yes, batching and cache TTL are orthogonal — we can change them on the routing policy. we can do an A/B test: 50% of traffic follows conservative path, 50% the current.
[05:36] Sofia Nguyen: we'll provision two routes: route-a (low-latency config) and route-b (cost-optimized). route-a will pin you to the rollback kernel if needed.

[06:00] -- Security and compliance checklist --
[06:06] Hannah Lee: we need SOC2 artifacts and the last five months of audit logs for the Private plane. also your KMS integration details — how keys are stored when we use HSM via our provider.
[06:15] Sofia Nguyen: okay. action: Sofia to share SOC2 summary, KMS/HSM integration doc, and the audit-log retention options. those docs will be shared by 2026-07-12.
[06:24] Carlos Mendes: one more: will logs be forwarded through our SIEM or do you want to ingest them into Redwood console only?
[06:30] Priya Rao: we support both; we'll provide a Logstash/Fluent config to forward to your SIEM.

[06:50] -- Deep-dive: kernel rollback plan (Luca) --
[06:54] Luca Martens: ok, technical runbook overview: pre-checks (health, cache warmness), canary strategy (10/30/100), monitoring probes (latency, error rate, KV cache miss rate), rollback criteria (95th > threshold OR error-rate > baseline + 2x), and post-checks (data-plane integrity).
[07:12] Daniel Ruiz: what about long-lived connections? do clients need to reconnect?
[07:16] Luca Martens: no, the proxy handles connection drain; the worker restarts will cause short REQs to reconnect; we recommend drain timeout 120s.
[07:22] Maya Patel: if we see any PII exposure during debug logs we will trigger immediate rollback and rotate keys.
[07:28] Hannah Lee: agreed.

[07:45] -- Conversation turns to calibration results --
[07:48] Luca Martens: uploaded spreadsheet to the shared drive — LiveBench_v4 — shows batch=8 lowers 95th by ~80ms on average for clinical prompts; throughput drops ~12% but cost delta is small given the SLO.
[08:02] Sofia Nguyen: link in the chat now: https://redwood.app/sheets/LiveBench_v4 (note: placeholder link).
[08:08] Maya Patel: looking — ok that aligns with our expectations. can Luca also run the same with the rollback kernel? we want direct comparison.
[08:15] Luca Martens: yes, that's in my next-sweep queue.

[08:30] -- Misc notes (imperfect transcription): --
[08:32] Speaker 1: um yeah I think the egress DNS rotation uh needs the, the cert pinning to be e-e-err...,
[08:40] Speaker 2: yeah we saw the CDN host swap and our firewall only allowed the old CIDR so that dropped telemetry,
[08:45] Speaker 3: "kv cahche" spelled as K-V cache sometimes in the logs so watch for that,

[09:00] -- Customer questions & objections --
[09:03] Daniel Ruiz: cost — if we roll back, what's the expected monthly delta?
[09:07] Sofia Nguyen: rough ballpark: +8-12% on token compute cost. we'll provide granular estimate after Luca's benchmark.
[09:14] Daniel Ruiz: and for routing changes, will you provide an audit trail?
[09:18] Priya Rao: yes, console shows rollout history and timestamps; we'll export an audit report for your compliance team.

[09:35] Hannah Lee: one ask — can we get a temporary read-only console view for our SecOps so they can inspect traces without risk?
[09:43] Sofia Nguyen: yes, we can create a read-only RBAC role scoped to your account.

[10:00] -- Scheduling & orchestration --
[10:04] Maya Patel: let's aim for the rollback window on Friday 2026-07-16 02:00 UTC. we need the docs beforehand and a dry run in staging next Tuesday.
[10:14] Sofia Nguyen: scheduled dry run Tuesday 2026-07-13 16:00 UTC — Luca, you'll lead; Priya on runbook; Arcwell will confirm staging subnet.
[10:24] Luca Martens: confirmed. I'll coordinate the run and post a check-list.

[10:40] -- Quick technical aside about CDN and ephemeral IPs (slight crosstalk) --
[10:44] Carlos Mendes: our firewall rules are CIDR based and AWS uses ephemeral egress from the NAT. we prefer prefixes so reduce churn.
[10:53] Sofia Nguyen: we'll provide static egress ranges for the control plane and note the ephemeral data-plane ranges; for Private we can put an egress proxy inside the VPC to keep IPs stable.

[11:12] -- Action recap (verbatim) --
[11:15] Sofia Nguyen: action items — I'll share SOC2 + KMS doc + network diagram by Sunday 2026-07-12. Luca will run two latency sweeps (rollback kernel + current) and upload results by 2026-07-14. Maya will validate egress rules in staging by 2026-07-13. Daniel to provision the isolated test subnet by 2026-07-15. Dry run scheduled for 2026-07-13 16:00 UTC. rollback target 2026-07-16 02:00 UTC.
[11:44] Maya Patel: sounds good. thanks.

[12:00] -- Closing --
[12:04] Sofia Nguyen: Appreciate the time. we'll follow up in email with the docs and meeting notes. any final quick questions?
[12:10] Hannah Lee: none from SecOps.
[12:12] Daniel Ruiz: all set.
[12:15] Sofia Nguyen: thanks everyone, bye.

End of transcript."
